head: 7610c6b22bcb8a46ea0ec2a9bd668b5fd02c6976
summary:
I tested the list on the real C:\ drive. It works as designed on everything I could reach except one layout state, which I measured on C:\ and which is still unfixed (O-024).

I published a fresh single-file exe from HEAD 7610c6b (139,791,512 bytes) and scanned C:\ through eng/read-window.ps1 as an ordinary user: 3,580,356 files, 827,367 folders, 664 unreadable folders.
- The report says 100 rows are bound, the list is inView, 5 rows are realized, and the caption reads 'Top 100 of 35,80,356 files scanned. Files in 664 unreadable folders are not included.'
- The first row is 55,430,873,088 bytes on disk. A separate in-memory .NET walk of C:\ agrees: its largest file is C:\Users\sshub\AppData\Local\Docker\wsl\disk\docker_data.vhdx at exactly that size, followed by pagefile.sys (21,474,836,480) and hiberfil.sys (13,439,676,416).
- largestFilesMs was 28.25 ms, and 26.90 ms on a second real scan. Both are under the 100 ms threshold that O-021 set for moving Top off the UI thread, so it stays where it is.

Other checks passed:
- The xUnit suite: 166/166.
- Fitness: all 26 rules hold.
- rules-parity: AGREE.
- WindowCases -Case All: 21/21 passed, 0 failed checks, including L-001 to L-006.

O-001 is verified by reading the code:
- Scanner.Scan runs the whole walk on the calling thread and returns only after Run.Execute returns and the SynchronousIoCancel guard is disposed, which joins its canceller thread.
- Every write to the store is a member of Run on that thread. The canceller only calls CancelSynchronousIo, and the pool thread only disposes handles.
- The app awaits the scan task before ShowOutcome calls ShowLargestFiles.

What fails is O-024, which is owed to build-slice. I opened the unreadable-folders expander on a real C:\ scan using a throwaway startup hook in %TEMP%, since deleted. At the default 880x600 window, LargestFilesPanel drops to 0 px and LargestFilesList is out of view, so on the main use case one click on '664 folders could not be read' hides the whole list. For that reason I grade criterion 11 as not met.

Criterion 14 (a probe-failed, open-and-growing or online-only file as a row) is not checked on a real list. The report carries no per-row flags or paths, so I could not tell whether any such file was in the list.

There is no loop: build attempt 1 failed and attempt 2 passed after changing tests only. The design's open questions are still undecided, and the real list shows them concretely: a Docker vhdx, pagefile.sys and hiberfil.sys lead C:\.

No 'What this slice owes' block was given, so `planned` is empty and the 14 design cases are graded under `criteria`.

checks.what: Fresh single-file self-contained publish from HEAD (the stack's 'verified by one real publish at validate')
checks.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 publish src/FsAnalyser.App/FsAnalyser.App.csproj -c Release -o artifacts/publish
checks.evidence: PUBLISH EXIT 0; artifacts/publish/FsAnalyser.App.exe 139,791,512 bytes, rewritten 19:53:36 local; only .pdb files beside it

checks.what: Core xUnit suite, including LargestFilesTests (8 Facts) and LargestFilesScaleTests
checks.evidence: Passed! - Failed: 0, Passed: 166, Skipped: 0, Total: 166, Duration: 10 s
26 rule(s) checked against 59 file(s); every declared rule holds
rules-parity: AGREE 8 facts <- 11 twinned entries, 23 patterns; exit 0

checks.what: O-001: nothing writes the store while Top reads it (read Scanner.cs, SynchronousIoCancel.cs, MainWindow.xaml.cs)
checks.command: Read src/FsAnalyser.Core/Scanning/Scanner.cs:12-38,71-95; Grep _store writers; Read SynchronousIoCancel.cs:216-301; Read MainWindow.xaml.cs:159-193,274-322
checks.evidence: Scan builds Run with 'using var io'/'using var run' and returns run.Execute() on the calling thread. All store writes (AppendRoot, SetChildren, AddFlags, Append, TryAddFileId, CorrectSizes at Scanner.cs:125-270) happen inside Run on that thread. The only other threads in Core are the canceller (CancelSynchronousIo only, joined in Dispose) and a pool thread that only disposes an aborted handle. The app awaits the LongRunning scan task (MainWindow.xaml.cs:159) before ShowOutcome and ShowLargestFiles run (:193, :320).

checks.what: Real C:\ scan through the published exe in report mode (the slice's main use case)
checks.evidence: EXIT 0; core Completed, files 3,580,356, folders 827,367, links 20,459, 211.3 s; largestFilesShown 100, largestFileOnDisk 55,430,873,088, largestFilesMs 28.2549; LargestFilesPanel visible 172.58 px; LargestFilesList 116.7 px inView true, realizedRows 5; UnreadableExpander visible, collapsed, inView true; caption 'Top 100 of 35,80,356 files scanned. Files in 664 unreadable folders are not included.'

checks.what: Independent reference for the real list's first row: an in-memory .NET FileSystemEnumerable walk of C:\ (reparse points skipped, inaccessible ignored, hidden and system files included), top 25 by logical size
checks.evidence: The walk took 62 s. #1 is C:\Users\sshub\AppData\Local\Docker\wsl\disk\docker_data.vhdx at 55,430,873,088, equal to the app's largestFileOnDisk (cluster-aligned, so on-disk equals logical). #2 is C:\pagefile.sys (21,474,836,480) and #3 C:\hiberfil.sys (13,439,676,416). Caveat: this walk counted 2,544,046 files against the app's 3,580,356. I did not investigate the gap; it is the reference walk's undercount, and its maximum still agrees.

checks.what: All default window cases on the fresh exe (L-001 to L-006 are SL-040's)
checks.evidence: CASES EXIT 0 in 3:50. PASSED: C-001 to C-014, O-016, L-001 to L-006; 282 'ok' lines and 0 failures. L-003: 7 of 100 rows built, surrogate row drawn (exit 0), LargestFilesPanel 226.46 px. L-005: stopped with 3 rows and the matching caption. L-006: both shapes, 'started ... largest=False rows=0'.

checks.what: O-024 on the real drive: the person opens the unreadable-folders expander on a C:\ outcome at the default window size
checks.command: Throwaway DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS dll built in %TEMP%\sl040-validate-hook (it subscribes to EndingShown and sets UnreadableExpander.IsExpanded=true), exe launched with 'C:\\ --report <file>' through ProcessStartInfo with the hook set for that one process only; the folder was deleted afterwards
checks.evidence: EXIT 0 after 2:40; hook log 'ending expander visibility=Visible expanded=True window=880x600'. Report: UnreadableExpander 205.58 px inView true; LargestFilesPanel visible with actualHeight 0; LargestFilesList inView false (realizedRows 3, 100 bound). The whole largest-files list is pushed out of view. Second real measurement: largestFilesMs 26.9034, largestFileOnDisk 55,430,873,088 again.

checks.what: Network window cases N-001 to N-004
checks.evidence: They change this machine's SMB client mappings. They are SL-038's cases, and nothing in this slice touches that path.

checks.what: Rules harness plants F17 to F19 (each analysis-rule plant fires in both engines)
checks.evidence: Code review ran them and recorded that they fire. Fitness and rules-parity pass on this tree. I did not re-run the harness.

checks.what: Row-by-row comparison of the real C:\ list's 100 paths against a reference
checks.evidence: The report deliberately carries no paths (Q-016). Only row 0's on-disk bytes and the row count are machine-readable from the shipped exe.

checks.what: Elevated read of the 664 unreadable folders (read-denied-folders)
checks.evidence: Not requested. The operation returns counts, never names or sizes, so it cannot tell whether a bigger file is hidden there. The caption already says those folders are excluded.

criteria.criterion: 1. rank the largest files under the scanned root: files at the top level and six folders down, where a folder's total is larger than any single file
criteria.how: LargestFilesTests.RanksFilesAtAnyDepthAndNeverAFolder passed (deep 3 MiB file first, 5 MiB folder never listed). On real C:\ the first row (55,430,873,088 bytes) is the independent walk's largest file, 7 folders down (AppData\Local\Docker\wsl\disk).

criteria.criterion: 2. cap the list at count: 105 files, count 100, ties at the cut
criteria.how: KeepsExactlyTheCountLargestWhenSizesTieAtTheCut passed (exactly 100 rows, no duplicate paths, equal to a full sort's first 100). L-003 shows 'Top 100 of 105'. Real C:\ shows 100.

criteria.criterion: 3. list a tree that has nothing to rank
criteria.how: ATreeWithNothingToRankGivesAnEmptyList passed. L-004 passed: caption 'No non-empty files found.', 0 rows, largestFileOnDisk null.

criteria.criterion: 4. list a file that has more than one name (3 MiB, second hardlink elsewhere)
criteria.how: AFileWithTwoNamesIsListedOnce passed: the second name is confirmed HardlinkDuplicate, and the list is [first name at 3 MiB, other].

criteria.criterion: 5. list files reached through links (file symlink, folder symlink, junction)
criteria.how: NoRowComesFromALink passed: all three are recorded as Link, and the only row is the 2 MiB target. Links are really created (Developer Mode, Q-001), never skipped.

criteria.criterion: 6. rank by space on disk with both sizes shown (64 MiB sparse vs 1 MiB dense)
criteria.how: RanksBySpaceOnDiskAndKeepsBothSizes passed: dense ranks first, and the sparse row has 64 MiB logical and at most 4 KiB on disk. The XAML shows 'On disk' and 'Size' columns under 'Largest files, by space on disk'.

criteria.criterion: 7. show where a file is (path >260 chars, trailing dot, trailing space, unpaired surrogate)
criteria.how: EachPathIsTheFilesExactPath passed: exact strings, no U+FFFD, File.Exists through \\?\. L-003 drew the surrogate row 0 and the exe exited 0 with a report. No human looked at how the text renders.

criteria.criterion: 8. list from a scan that was stopped
criteria.how: AStoppedScanListsOnlyWhatItRead passed. L-005 passed (Cancelled, 3 rows, caption '... in the part read before the scan stopped.'). The writer invariant was verified by reading Scanner.cs (O-001).

criteria.criterion: 9. start another scan after a list has been shown
criteria.how: L-006 passed in both shapes. Missing root: the list collapses with 0 rows at scan start and stays hidden at the failure ending. Begun: 0 rows at start, report core null.

criteria.criterion: 10. state what the list does not cover (biggest file in an unreadable folder)
criteria.how: L-002 passed (caption '... Files in 1 unreadable folder are not included.', the hidden 2 MiB file absent). AFileInAFolderTheScanCouldNotReadIsNotListed passed. On real C:\ the caption names 664 unreadable folders.

criteria.criterion: 11. fit the list into the outcome panel: 100 rows, a surrogate row, with the unreadable-folders list also filled
criteria.how: Collapsed expander (the state ShowOutcome leaves): L-003 passed, and on real C:\ LargestFilesList is 116.7 px and inView. Once the person opens the filled unreadable list at the default 880x600 window on real C:\, LargestFilesPanel is 0 px and LargestFilesList inView is false. This is the defect O-024 records, still unfixed at HEAD 7610c6b.

criteria.criterion: 12. report what the window shows after a finished scan of a planted tree
criteria.how: L-001 passed (3 rows, largestFileOnDisk 327680, largestFilesMs measured, no planted name in the report). The real C:\ report carries the same keys with sane values and no paths.

criteria.criterion: 13. rank a very large scan (4-5 million entries)
criteria.how: Real C:\ store of about 4.43 million entries: largestFilesMs 28.25 ms and 26.90 ms on two scans, under the 100 ms Task.Run threshold O-021 set. LargestFilesScaleTests (4,417,469 synthetic entries, under 1 MiB allocated) passed.

criteria.criterion: 14. rank a file whose size the scanner had to probe (open and growing, probe failed, online-only placeholder)
criteria.how: The design marks this case material:false and relies on the sparse test, the spike open-growing-file-stale-directory-size and OnDiskSizeTests. The real C:\ list was produced without error, but the report has no per-row flags or paths, so I could not tell whether any probe-failed, open-and-growing or online-only file was a row.

obligations.evidence: Scanner.cs:12 walks depth-first on the caller's thread. Scanner.cs:30-38 returns run.Execute() inside 'using var io'/'using var run', and SynchronousIoCancel.Dispose (:216-229) joins the canceller before Scan returns. Every store writer is called only from Run (Scanner.cs:125-270). The canceller thread only calls CancelSynchronousIo, and the pool thread in Close (:159-179) only disposes a SafeFileHandle. MainWindow.xaml.cs:159 awaits the scan task before ShowOutcome and ShowLargestFiles (:193, :320). So the ranking key cannot change during the pass for Completed or Cancelled scans. AStoppedScanListsOnlyWhatItRead and L-005 also passed.

Owed to build-slice and still open: HEAD is 7610c6b, the reviewed commit, and MainWindow.xaml is unchanged. Reproduced on the real C:\ drive: with UnreadableExpander opened (throwaway startup hook) at 880x600, UnreadableExpander is 205.58 px and LargestFilesPanel 0 px, with LargestFilesList inView false. On C:\ the list disappears entirely, which is worse than the reviewer's 26 px on a 12-folder temp tree.

not_reached: Paths of the real C:\ list's 100 rows: the report carries no paths by design (Q-016), so only row 0's size and the row count were compared with an independent reference. The other 99 rows and their shown locations were not read.
No person looked at the window. How wrapped 400-character paths, a lone-surrogate name, and the 'On disk'/'Size' columns look was judged only from report metrics (inView, heights, realized rows).

Criterion 14's probe shapes on a real list: whether an online-only OneDrive placeholder, a probe-failed system file or an open-and-growing file appears with correct values as a row. I did not open the person's OneDrive folder.
The contents of the 664 unreadable folders on C:\: the list cannot include them, and read-denied-folders returns counts only, so it could not say whether a larger file is hidden there.
Windows 10, other DPI settings, and window sizes other than the default 880x600; only Windows 11 build 26200 was exercised.
Drives other than NTFS C:\ (exFAT/FAT removable, mapped SMB share) with the list shown.
Why the independent .NET walk counted about 1.04M fewer files than the scanner (2,544,046 vs 3,580,356). It did not affect the row-0 comparison, and it is not this slice's code.
